newsitem.title: UK: Key world closing stock market indices, Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: Key world closing stock market indices, Feb 7.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - Shares soared to a record finish -- the second time this week and eighth time in the first six weeks of 1997 -- as investors continued to believe interest rates on both sides of the Atlantic would not rise in the near-term. The FTSE 100 index closed 41.9 points higher at 4,307.8, up 32 points since the start of the week.

FRANKFURT - Bulls ran rampant in electronic share trade during the afternoon as the dollar penetrated the 1.67-mark threshold and the Dow Jones Industrial index opened sharply higher to underpin lively IBIS DAX trade. The IBIS DAX index of electronic trade continued its record-breaking run to end the day at an all-time closing high of 3,161.36 points. Earlier, the DAX index, which gauges bourse trade, also ended on a record high at 3,138.01 points, up 33.87 points on the day and 102.86 since last Friday.

PARIS - Stocks set a third consecutive closing record after rallying on the back of a strong rise on Wall Street and a U.S. jobs report that eased financial markets' interest-rate fears. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 39.09 points, or 1.53 percent, at 2,597.52. This week the CAC-40 gained 75.64 points.

ZURICH - Shares ended this week's relentless record run with with another high, jumping more than one percent on favourable U.S. job data, a rising U.S. dollar and a strong Wall Street opening. The all-share SPI was up 29.86 points to 2,783.25 a gain of 54.92 on the week.

TOKYO - Stocks ended down after the construction sector came under heavy fire due to rumours about the financial stability of Tobishima Corp, which the firm later denied . The 225-share Nikkei average ended down 171.39 points at 17,867.04 a fall of 462.97 from last Friday's close.

HONG KONG - The stock market was closed again today for the Chinese lunar new year holiday. On Wednesday, the Hang Seng index closed 112.07 points higher at 13,660.50, gaining 338.71 points from last Friday. The market will reopen on February 10.

SYDNEY - A fiesty share market fought its way to a record close, extending the resilient rearguard action started on Thursday afternoon as stocks eked out modest gains in most sectors. The finish surpasses the previous record close of 2,444.2, reached on January 20, 1997. The All Ordinaries index added 11.5 points to 2,446.7 a gain of 23 points on the week.
JOHANNESBURG - Shares closed up, despite a slide in the gold index, as positive sentiment continued to support the market.
President Nelson Mandela's speech at the opening of parliament in Cape Town contained no surprises and was seen underpinning a recent upsurge in confidence -- without triggering off a major rally.

The all-share index ended up 16.0 points to 6,879.6, a gain of 203.5 since last Friday, as the industrial index put on 22.6 points to 8,203.0 up 199.7 on the week. But the gold index took a hammering as the bullion price dropped to its lowest levels for nearly four years. The index shed 30.0 points, or 2.16 percent, to 1,357.5 up 7.5 from last weeks close.
